subject: Catalyst Systems — Technical onboarding & integration sprint plan
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@catalystsys.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@catalystsys.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood integration kickoff + tech validation scope

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week; Catalyst is excited to move forward. We'd like to kick off a short technical onboarding + validation sprint so our engineering and security teams can validate the reference design and prove a small POC that exercises the following:

- Model serving modes: hosted vs dedicated behavior for multi-tenant workloads
- Latency and cost profile for our 1k qps simulated load (short-seq & long-seq mixes)
- Auth and audit flows (SSO, API keys, and audit logs preservation)
- Data residency (we plan to deploy in the us-west region)
- Quantized model variants and any recommended config for our LLMs (we'll provide model artifacts)

Can we scope a 3-week validation sprint starting the week of Jun 21? We'd appreciate a simple runbook and a reference acceptance checklist. I've attached our onboarding checklist and a short list of security questions to that effect.

Proposed attendees from our side: Emily Park (eng lead), Carlos Ruiz (solutions), security@catalystsys.com (infosec).

Thanks — let me know if you want to kick off with a 30-min technical alignment first.

Best,
Emily
Emily Park
Head of Integrations, Catalyst Systems
Attachments: Catalyst_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@catalystsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + tech validation scope

Emily —

Great to hear and glad you're ready to move. 3-week sprint starting Jun 21 sounds doable. High-level plan:

1) Week 0 (alignment call, environment access): 30–45m alignment (Jun 21) to confirm endpoints, credentials, and test datasets.
2) Week 1 (reference deploy + smoke tests): deploy reference architecture in a dedicated test VPC (Redwood Private or Dedicated sandbox), run smoke and latency profiles.
3) Week 2 (load + acceptance): run scaled qps runs, quantify cost per 1k tokens and validate caching/batching improvements.
4) Week 3 (wrap, regressions, handoff): review results, document recommended quantization/profile settings, and produce acceptance report.

I've attached a Redwood reference architecture and an example runbook — Marissa will own the runbook and the smoke tests, Rishi owns security/compliance answers. We'll send a formal schedule after the quick alignment call.

Can you confirm Emily/Carlos availability for Jun 21 at 10:00 PDT or Jun 21 at 15:00 PDT?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
Attachments: redwood-reference-arch-v1.pdf (PDF, 310KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@catalystsys.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + tech validation scope

Hi Emily — looping in a draft of the tech runbook and acceptance checklist so you can review ahead of the call. Key items I've included:

- Reference deployment topology (hosted/dedicated/private variants) + resource sizing guidance for 1k qps target.
- Test harness: synthetic traffic generator config and sequence-length distributions.
- Acceptance criteria: <2x baseline latency for long seqs, successful fallback to smaller model variant under resource pressure, audit log retention >= 90 days in test env.
- Security gates: SSO (SAML/OIDC), IP allowlist, API key rotation demo, and KMS integration for private keys.

Notes / open questions for call:
- Will you be providing model artifacts as standard Hugging Face checkpoints or containerized images? That changes our onboarding steps (we can accept either).
- Do you require SOC2 evidence beyond the standard audit bundle?

I've attached the runbook stub and a list of proposed test cases. Happy to iterate.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-runbook-draft.md (text, 12KB)
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@catalystsys.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: security@catalystsys.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + tech validation scope

Thanks Marissa — quick Q from infosec:

1) SSO: we prefer SAML with encrypted assertions. Can Redwood support IdP-initiated SAML flows in a Private deployment?
2) Audit logs: can we get an exportable audit trail with token-level request IDs and timestamps for the test period? Format JSON/CSV preferred.
3) Data handling: for PII in requests, what are the recommended redaction transforms (client-side vs server-side)?

Also, on models: we'll provide container images for two model sizes (base and quantized) and we plan to exercise the smaller quantized variant for cost/perf comparisons.

—Carlos
Carlos Ruiz
Solutions Architect, Catalyst Systems
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@catalystsys.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration kickoff + tech validation scope

Carlos —

Short answers: yes, yes, and recommendations below.

SSO: Redwood Private supports IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML/OIDC flows. For Private deployments we can configure SAML assertions with encrypted attributes and map groups to RBAC roles. We'll add step-by-step SAML config to the runbook.

Audit logs: we can export request-level logs including request_id, timestamp, model, token counts, and latency. Exports can be delivered as newline-delimited JSON or CSV. We'll provision a temporary log export bucket for the sprint and hand off a filtered dataset on completion.

PII handling: our recommended pattern for this sprint is client-side tokenization/redaction for highest control. For added safety we support server-side redaction hooks in Redwood Private (pre-processing plugins) that can mask/strip fields. We'll document the sample redaction plugin and provide a small template you can run in the test env.

On the container images: thanks — containerized model images are ideal. Please share registry access or provide a downloadable tarball. We'll stage them in the dedicated sandbox and run quantized vs base comparisons.

I'll add these answers to the runbook and include sample SAML metadata.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@catalystsys.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@catalystsys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Draft runbook + proposed test matrix (please review)

Emily/Carlos —

Attached is the draft runbook (PDF & runbook stub) and the proposed test matrix. Highlights:

- Day 0: Access & artifact ingestion (we'll need registry creds or model tarballs by Jun 20).
- Day 1–3: Reference deploy + smoke tests (latency/functional).
- Day 4–8: Stress & load (synthetic harness to the 1k qps mix).
- Day 9–11: Quantized vs base model comparison and cost modeling.
- Day 12–14: Security verification, SAML integration, and audit export review.

Please review the attached test matrix and add any missing acceptance criteria. Also confirm whether you'd like us to run the load tests in Redwood Hosted (fastest path) or in a Dedicated sandbox (most representative for your SLA). My recommendation: run initial functional + load tests in Dedicated sandbox, and a short smoke run in Hosted to compare cold-start characteristics.

Proposed times for alignment call (all PST): Jun 21 10:00, Jun 21 15:00, Jun 22 09:00 — tell us what works.

Marissa
Attachments: redwood-runbook-draft.pdf (PDF, 250KB), test-matrix.csv (CSV, 18KB)

Emily/Carlos —

Thanks for the quick turn. Confirming Jun 21 at 10:00 PDT for the alignment call (we'll send a calendar invite). Agenda: 20m technical alignment (Marissa/Rishi), 10m logistics (me/Sergio), 5m next steps and owner assignments.

Action items before the call (Catalyst):
- Share registry credentials or model tarballs to the Drive link before EOD Jun 20.
- Mark security questions in the runbook and confirm whether you need SOC2 artifacts beyond our standard bundle.

Action items from Redwood:
- Marissa to finalize runbook and test matrix by Jun 20 (draft posted to Drive).
- Rishi to attach SAML metadata and sample redaction plugin.
- Sergio to prep a commercial note on sandbox capacity and cost estimate for Dedicated runs (will follow after call).

I'll include a short DocuSign link for the sandbox terms after the call if Catalyst wants the Dedicated sandbox reserved. Looking forward to the call.

Laura Bennett
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference runtime
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
